authentication.description: OAuth2 Bearer token or private API token passed via Authorization header

rate_limits.notes: Rate limits and usage caps are returned in response headers

identify.description: Segment maps identify calls to Drift contact create/update via the Contacts API. userId maps to externalId, traits map to contact attributes.

track.description: Segment maps track calls to Drift events. The event name and properties are forwarded to Drift's event tracking system, associated with the contact identified by userId or anonymousId.

expected_api_call.description: Track events are sent to Drift via the client-side drift.track() method or server-side event ingestion. Events are associated with the Drift contact matching the userId (externalId) or anonymousId (drift_aid).

identify.description: RudderStack maps identify calls to Drift contact create/update via the Contacts API, following the same pattern as Segment. userId maps to externalId, traits map to contact attributes. RudderStack adds envelope fields to the source event.

track.description: RudderStack maps track calls to Drift events, following the same pattern as Segment. The event name and properties are forwarded to Drift's event tracking system. RudderStack adds envelope fields to the source event.

expected_api_call.description: Track events are sent to Drift via the client-side drift.track() method or server-side event ingestion. Events are associated with the Drift contact matching the userId (externalId) or anonymousId (drift_aid).

userId_to_externalId.description: Segment userId maps to Drift externalId for contact deduplication. Drift uses externalId to uniquely identify contacts and prevent duplicates.

email.description: Email is the only required attribute when creating a Drift contact. Both platforms map traits.email to attributes.email.

name.description: Full name mapping. Drift also supports first_name and last_name as separate attributes.

first_name.description: First name mapping. Note case convention difference: Segment uses camelCase (firstName), Drift uses snake_case (first_name).
first_name.known_gap: Case convention transformation: camelCase to snake_case for Drift standard attributes

last_name.description: Last name mapping. Same case convention difference as first_name.
last_name.known_gap: Case convention transformation: camelCase to snake_case for Drift standard attributes

phone.description: Phone number mapping. Direct mapping between both platforms.

company.description: Company name mapping. Drift also has an Accounts API for more detailed company/ABM data.

custom_traits.description: Custom traits are mapped to custom Drift contact attributes. Drift auto-creates attributes on first use and infers data types. Attributes are case-sensitive and immutable once typed.
custom_traits.known_gap: Drift attribute type inference may differ from Segment trait types. Drift attributes are immutable once typed.

anonymousId_to_drift_aid.description: Segment anonymousId does not directly map to a Drift API field. Drift uses drift_aid cookie for anonymous visitor tracking. Server-side identify calls use externalId instead.
anonymousId_to_drift_aid.known_gap: No direct server-side equivalent for anonymousId in Drift. Drift assigns its own contactId for anonymous visitors.

event_name.description: Event name is passed as the first argument to drift.track(). Both platforms use the event name string directly.

properties.description: Event properties are passed as the second argument object to drift.track(). Properties map directly as key-value pairs.

userId_association.description: Track events are associated with the Drift contact matching the userId (externalId). The contact must be identified before events can be attributed.

timestamp.description: Drift events use the time of receipt rather than a client-provided timestamp. Segment provides a timestamp field that Drift may not honor for server-side events.
timestamp.known_gap: Drift may use server receipt time instead of the event timestamp provided by Segment/RudderStack

conversation_context.description: Drift conversations provide additional context that enriches event data. When events occur within a conversation context, Drift associates conversationId, inboxId, and participant data.

fields.inboxId: The inbox ID for the conversation
fields.endUserId: The Drift Contact ID of the end user
fields.endUserEmail: Email of the end user if known

conversation_context.notes: Conversation context fields are Drift-specific and not present in standard Segment/RudderStack event payloads. These are generated by Drift's Source integration, not the Destination integration.

identify_parity.description: Identify calls map cleanly to Drift Contacts API. Core field mappings (email, name, phone, company, externalId) are equivalent. Custom traits map to custom attributes with potential type inference differences.
known_gaps: Case convention: Segment camelCase traits vs Drift snake_case standard attributes
Attribute type immutability: Drift attributes cannot change type once set
anonymousId: No direct Drift server-side equivalent

track_parity.description: Track calls map to Drift's event tracking system. Event name and properties are forwarded. Timestamp handling and contact association method may differ.
known_gaps: Timestamp handling: Drift may use receipt time instead of event timestamp
Server-side track events require contact to be pre-identified via externalId
Drift event properties are used for segmentation, not stored as raw event history

destination_api_differences.segment_approach: Maps userId to externalId via Contacts API (POST/PATCH)
destination_api_differences.rudderstack_approach: Same mapping via Transformer service to Contacts API (POST/PATCH)
destination_api_differences.gap: Verify identical field transformation and error handling

destination_api_differences.segment_approach: Forwards track events to Drift's event system via client-side or server-side API
Custom traits auto-mapped to Drift custom attributes
destination_api_differences.rudderstack_approach: Custom traits auto-mapped to Drift custom attributes via Transformer
destination_api_differences.gap: Verify case convention handling and type coercion are identical

destination_api_differences.segment_approach: OAuth2 Bearer token from Drift app configuration
destination_api_differences.gap: Verify token format and header are equivalent

accessToken.description: Drift API access token (OAuth2 Bearer token or private API token)

identifyByEmail.description: When true, use email as the primary identifier for contact lookup instead of externalId

notes: Drift is a shared cloud destination in the Livechat category. Both Segment and RudderStack support identify and track calls to Drift. Drift's Contacts API (https://driftapi.com/contacts) handles contact creation and updates, while drift.track() handles event ingestion. Key parity areas to validate: (1) Contact attribute mapping from Segment/RudderStack traits to Drift attributes, (2) Event property serialization, (3) Case convention transformations for standard Drift attributes (camelCase to snake_case), (4) Handling of anonymous visitors without externalId. Drift also has a Source integration that sends events FROM Drift TO Segment, which is the reverse direction and not covered by this fixture. Rate limit: 600 requests/minute. Drift was acquired by Salesloft in 2024.
